newsitem.title: USA: Xerox unveils four digital printers.
newsitem.headline: Xerox unveils four digital printers.

text.p: Xerox Corp. unveiled Tuesday four new digital printers that it said were the fastest in their categories, operating at twice the speed of previous products.
Xerox presented the new printers at the On-Demand Digital Printing and Publishing Conference in New York just two weeks after it rolled out four high-speed digital copiers for computer networks.
The company said the new lines of printers and copiers were the first step in its overall strategy of focusing on digital products.

"We have raised the productiveness quotient in three product families that already command market leadership in high-speed digital printing -- DocuTech, DocuColor and DocuPrint," Chairman Paul A. Allaire said in a speech to the conference.
The four new printers were aimed at the digital production printing area, where Xerox already gets $5 billion in revenues.

The two black-and-white printers, the DocuTech 6180 Production Publisher and the DocuPrint 180 Enterprise Printing System, use Xerox's proprietary dual-beam laser technology, which enables higher-quality printing at a speed of 180 pages per minute.

The DocuTech 6180 is available immediately in select cities with phased rollouts in North America, Europe, Australia and Latin America throughout 1997. It carries a base price of $413,000. The DocuPrint 180 will be available in the beginning of the third quarter for a list price of $490,000.

"The DocuTech has been their flagship product for years," said Robert Fennell, an analyst with Dataquest Inc., a market research firm in San Jose, Calif. "They are really extending the product line. They are making major enhancements in the colour area."

Xerox also introduced two colour printers. One, the DocuColor 70 Digital Colour Production System, produces 70 high-quality, full-colour impressions per minute. Xerox said the system is the fastest digital colour production system.
The product builds on the launch in 1996 of the DocuColor 40, which has captured more than 50 percent of the market for short-run digital colour production, Xerox said.
The DocuColor 70 will be available in September in North America and Europe and in South America in the fourth quarter. The base price will be $375,000 to $390,000.
The second colour printer, the DocuPrint 184hc, will be available in the United States beginning June 30 for a list price of $490,000.
Xerox's stock gained 87.5 cents to $64.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
